text:
Abstract
The user requested every Escherichia coli heat-shock expression study with their accessions. I queried the NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE) dataset index restricted to the NCBI GEO catalog using the nde_search_datasets tool with the query "heat shock Escherichia coli", returning 42 matching Dataset records. I filtered those 42 records to retain entries that (a) mention "heat" or "heat shock" in the dataset name or description (case-insensitive) and (b) list Escherichia coli in the dataset's reported organisms/pathogens. This filter produced 13 datasets (13/42 = 31.0%). Table 1 lists the 13 GEO accessions, titles, and the exact GEO URLs returned by the search tool. These results matter because they provide a reproducible, tool-traceable list of GEO studies that explicitly couple E. coli and heat-shock conditions and so serve as a starting point for meta-analysis, re-use, or differential-expression re-analysis.

I. Introduction
Background. Heat-shock responses in Escherichia coli are central to proteostasis and survival under elevated temperatures; transcriptomic and translational profiling under heat stress reveal regulons (e.g., sigma32/rpoH targets) and mechanisms of thermotolerance. Researchers frequently deposit expression datasets in NCBI GEO (GSE accessions).

Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.

Knowledge Gap. A concise, tool-traceable list of GEO accessions that specifically pair E. coli and heat-shock expression experiments was not compiled prior to this query.

Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: compile every E. coli heat-shock expression Dataset (GEO accessions) discoverable by the NDE index under the query "heat shock Escherichia coli". Hypothesis: the NDE search will return GEO datasets that explicitly mention heat shock and Escherichia coli; filtering by those criteria will produce a reproducible list of accessions.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. I used a single federated search against the NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE) dataset index restricted to NCBI GEO to retrieve candidate datasets, then filtered the returned records by text-matching "heat" (case-insensitive) in the dataset name or description and by the presence of "Escherichia coli" in the dataset's reported organisms/pathogens.

Materials. Tool and database:
- nde_search_datasets (NIAID Data Ecosystem index; restricted to NCBI GEO records)

Procedures. I executed one tool call:
1) nde_search_datasets with parameters:
   - query: "heat shock Escherichia coli"
   - repository: "NCBI GEO"
   - record_type: "Dataset"
   - size: 500

(Exact tool call and returned metadata are documented in the References section as the API provenance.)

Post-processing (filtering) steps (performed on the tool output):
- From the returned list of 42 Dataset records (the tool's "total" = 42), select records where:
  a) the dataset "name" OR "description" contained the substring "heat" (case-ins.) — i.e., any occurrence of "heat" (this captures "heat shock", "heat stress", etc.); AND
  b) the dataset's "pathogens" (organism list) included "Escherichia coli" (as shown in the returned record).

Statistical Analysis. Counts were taken from the NDE tool response fields:
- Denominator: total number of Dataset records returned by the search (the tool's "total" field) = 42.
- Numerator: number of returned records meeting the two filtering criteria above = 13.
- Percentage = (13 / 42) × 100 = 31.0% (rounded to three significant digits).
- No deduplication beyond the unique GSE accession strings returned by the NDE results was necessary; every accession in Table 1 is unique in the returned list.

III. Results
Data Presentation.

Table 1 — GEO accessions returned by the NDE search, filtered to datasets that mention "heat" (name or description) and that report Escherichia coli among organisms/pathogens. The URLs are the exact GEO accession pages provided in each record's links.

| GEO accession | Dataset title (as returned) | GEO record URL |
|---|---:|---|
| GSE85807 | Transcriptomic changes of Escherichia coli expressing BnTR1 at normal and heat stress conditions | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE85807 |
| GSE90056 | Translation efficiency is maintained during heat shock in Escherichia coli | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE90056 |
| GSE11463 | Transcriptome analysis of Escherichia coli O157:H7 EDL933 during heat shock using microarrays | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE11463 |
| GSE144942 | Azidonucleoside-incorporated RNA sequencing for new transcripts analysis under heat shock in E.coli | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE144942 |
| GSE33212 | Transcriptome analysis of MDS42 and MG1655 (includes heat shock comparisons) | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE33212 |
| GSE216100 | Structure of Escherichia coli heat shock protein Hsp15 in complex with ribosomal 50S sununits bearing peptidyl-tRNA | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE216100 |
| GSE27607 | Determinants of heat resistance in Escherichia coli AW1.7 | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE27607 |
| GSE330026 | The GndA microprotein promotes cell growth during heat shock | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE330026 |
| GSE269907 | Cellular function of the GndA small open reading frame-encoded polypeptide during heat shock | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE269907 |
| GSE299621 | eIF3g binding to GUCG boxes spread in mRNA coding regions mediates translational heat shock response | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE299621 |
| GSE61749 | Transcriptome analysis of thermal adaptive E. coli (part 1) (includes response to heat shock) | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE61749 |
| GSE15534 | Transcriptome analysis of E.coli MG1655 under multiple growth conditions (includes heat shock) | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE15534 |
| GSE13698 | 12 microarrays for cis-DCE mineralization and new stress genes (description reports strong heat shock and/or oxidative stress) | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE13698 |

Findings. From the NDE search:
- Total returned candidate GEO Datasets: 42.
- Datasets matching the filtering criteria ("heat" in name/description AND Escherichia coli listed): 13.
- Proportion: 13/42 = 31.0%.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The NDE search for "heat shock Escherichia coli" returned 42 GEO Dataset records; text- and organism-based filtering identified 13 datasets that explicitly couple Escherichia coli with heat stress or heat-shock conditions in the title or description. These 13 GSE accessions form a reproducible, tool-traceable list suitable for downstream retrieval of raw/processed data (via the GEO URLs) for meta-analysis or re-analysis.

Context. The listed records include microarray, tiling-array, ribosome-profiling, and RNA-seq style datasets and span different E. coli strains (K-12, MG1655, O157:H7) and experimental foci (whole-transcriptome, translational control, small open reading frames, thermotolerance determinants). The source of the results is the NIAID Data Ecosystem aggregated index (NDE) querying the NCBI GEO catalog; each row in Table 1 links to the GEO accession page returned by that index.

Limitations.
- Query dependence: the result set depends on the literal query "heat shock Escherichia coli". Datasets that are relevant but which do not include the term "heat" or that phrase in the indexed title/description or that omit "Escherichia coli" from the indexed organism list will be missed.
- Indexing coverage and metadata: NDE index extraction of organism keywords and descriptions can vary; some multi-organism studies or host–microbe studies list multiple taxa and the primary organism may not be E. coli even if E. coli appears in the record, so manual inspection of each GEO page is recommended before reuse.
- Scope: I only searched NDE restricted to the NCBI GEO repository. Other repositories (ArrayExpress, SRA project pages) were not included.
- No PubMed/literature verification was performed; biological interpretation (e.g., which datasets are true "expression" vs. structural or other assay types) requires reading the GEO record and associated publications.

Conclusion & Future Directions. I provide a reproducible list of 13 GEO accessions that the NDE index returned and that explicitly link Escherichia coli with heat/heat-shock conditions in their metadata. Next useful queries: (a) fetch each GEO record to list the sample-level platforms and raw data files (GSM and SRA links) for pipeline planning; (b) broaden the search to include related terms ("heat stress", "thermotolerance", "temperature shift") and additional repositories (SRA, ArrayExpress); (c) run automated retrieval and collate sample metadata for a combined meta-analysis.

References
[1] NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE) — API call used (provenance): https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=%28heat+shock+Escherichia+coli%29+AND+%40type%3A%22Dataset%22+AND+includedInDataCatalog.name%3A%22NCBI+GEO%22&size=500&_source=_id%2C%40type%2Cname%2Cdescription%2Curl%2Cdoi%2Cidentifier%2Cdate%2CdatePublished%2CdateModified%2CincludedInDataCatalog.name%2CincludedInDataCatalog.url%2CincludedInDataCatalog.archivedAt%2Cauthor.name%2CinfectiousAgent.name%2CinfectiousAgent.displayName%2Cspecies.name%2ChealthCondition.name%2CmeasurementTechnique.name%2CtopicCategory.name%2Ckeywords%2CconditionsOfAccess%2Clicense%2Cdistribution.contentUrl%2CsourceOrganization.name%2Cfunding.funder.name%2CprogrammingLanguage%2CapplicationCategory%2CoperatingSystem%2CsoftwareVersion%2CcodeRepository%2CisBasedOn.identifier%2CvariableMeasured.name%2Cvalue%2CunitText%2CmarginOfError.name%2CmarginOfError.value%2CobservationAbout.name%2CobservationAbout.identifier%2CmeasuredProperty.name%2CobservationType.name%2CmeasurementQualifier%2CsubjectOf.identifier
